# Data dictionary

**EMS Incident Dispatch Data** (NYC Open Data `76xm-jjuj`, FDNY). The EMS Incident Dispatch Data file contains data that is generated by the EMS Computer Aided Dispatch System. The data spans from the time the incident is created in the system to the time the incident is closed in the system.  It covers information about the incident as it relates to the assignment of resources and the Fire Department’s response to the emergency. To protect personal identifying information in accordance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), specific locations of incidents are not included and have been aggregated to a higher level of detail.

Field types come from the Socrata columns API; descriptions come from the dataset's official attachment `EMS_incident_dispatch_data_description.xlsx`. Generated by `src/dictionary.py`.

## Source fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `incident_id` | text | Unique identifier for each incident which serves as the Primary Key |
| `incident_datetime` | calendar_date | The date and time the incident was created in the dispatch system |
| `initial_call_type` | text | The call type assigned at the time of incident creation. Note: The call type does not reflect the actual condition of the patient.  It is a determination based on information obtained from the caller for the purpose of defining severity and resource allocation. |
| `initial_severity_level_code` | text | The segment(priority) assigned at the time of incident creation. |
| `final_call_type` | text | The call type at the time the incident closes. Note: The call type does not reflect the actual condition of the patient.  It is a determination based on information obtained from the caller for the purpose of defining severity and resource allocation. The call type does not change based on the findings of the on scene ambulance crew. |
| `final_severity_level_code` | text | The segment(priority) assigned at the time the incident closes. |
| `first_assignment_datetime` | calendar_date | The date and time the first unit is assigned. |
| `valid_dispatch_rspns_time_indc` | text | Indicates that the components comprising the calculation of the DISPATCH_RESPONSE_SECONDS_QY are valid. |
| `dispatch_response_seconds_qy` | number | The time elapsed in seconds between the incident_datetime and the first_assignment_datetime. |
| `first_activation_datetime` | calendar_date | The date and time the first unit gives the signal that it is enroute to the location of the incident. |
| `first_on_scene_datetime` | calendar_date | The date and time the first unit signals that it has arrived at the location of the incident. |
| `valid_incident_rspns_time_indc` | text | Indicates that the components comprising the calculation of the INCIDENT_RESPONSE_SECONDS_QY are valid. |
| `incident_response_seconds_qy` | number | The time elapsed in seconds between the incident_datetime and the first_on_scene_datetime. |
| `incident_travel_tm_seconds_qy` | number | The time elapsed in seconds between the first_assignment_datetime and the first_on_scene_datetime. |
| `first_to_hosp_datetime` | calendar_date | The date and time the first unit gives the signal that it is enroute to the hospital. |
| `first_hosp_arrival_datetime` | calendar_date | The date and time the first unit signals that it has arrived at the hospital. |
| `incident_close_datetime` | calendar_date | The date and time the incident closes in the dispatch system. |
| `held_indicator` | text | Indicates that for some reason a unit could not be assigned immediately |
| `incident_disposition_code` | text | A code indicating the final outcome of the incident. See incident dispositions. |
| `borough` | text | The borough of the incident location. |
| `incident_dispatch_area` | text | The dispatch area of the incident. |
| `zipcode` | text | The zip code of the incident. |
| `policeprecinct` | number | The police precinct of the incident. |
| `citycouncildistrict` | number | The city council district. |
| `communitydistrict` | number | The community district. |
| `communityschooldistrict` | number | The community school district. |
| `congressionaldistrict` | number | The congressional district. |
| `reopen_indicator` | text | Indicates that at some point the incident was closed but then reopened. |
| `special_event_indicator` | text | Indicates that the incident was a special event such as the NYC Marathon. |
| `standby_indicator` | text | Indicates that the units were assigned to stand by incase they were needed. |
| `transfer_indicator` | text | Indicates that the incident was created for the  transportation of a patient from one facility (ie a hospital or nursing home) to another. |

## Derived fields (src/clean.py)

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| `call_handling_s` | incident_datetime → first_assignment_datetime. Time from the incident being created in the EMS dispatch system to the first unit being assigned. Equals DISPATCH_RESPONSE_SECONDS_QY. Includes any time the call was held because no unit was free. |
| `dispatch_s` | first_assignment_datetime → first_activation_datetime. Time from assignment to the unit signalling it is en route. |
| `travel_s` | first_activation_datetime → first_on_scene_datetime. Driving time from en route to on scene. |
| `response_s` | incident_datetime → first_on_scene_datetime = call_handling_s + dispatch_s + travel_s. Equals INCIDENT_RESPONSE_SECONDS_QY. |
| `life_threatening` | initial_severity_level_code in 1, 2, 3. |
| `modzcta` | Modified ZIP Code Tabulation Area the incident zip belongs to (from the MODZCTA 'zcta' list). |
| `rt_ok` | Row passes every response-time cleaning rule (see docs/data_quality.md). |

## Response-time breakdown

The dataset has no timestamp for when the 911 call was answered, so the breakdown starts when the incident is created in the EMS dispatch system. The three parts used everywhere in this project are:

1. **Call handling**: incident created → first unit assigned (`call_handling_s`).
2. **Dispatch**: unit assigned → unit en route (`dispatch_s`).
3. **Travel**: unit en route → first unit on scene (`travel_s`).

Note the dataset's own `incident_travel_tm_seconds_qy` runs from assignment to on scene, so it equals dispatch + travel here.

## Severity and the life-threatening definition

Severity codes are FDNY dispatch segments 1 (most urgent) to 8 (least). FDNY and the Mayor's Management Report treat segments 1-3 as life-threatening medical emergencies (for example cardiac arrest, choking, major asthma, difficulty breathing, stroke). This project defines a life-threatening call as `initial_severity_level_code` in {1, 2, 3}: the initial segment is what the dispatcher knew when choosing how fast to send a unit. `life_threatening_final` uses the final segment instead and is kept for sensitivity checks.

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| 82 | transporting patient |
| 83 | patient pronounced dead |
| 87 | cancelled |
| 90 | unfounded |
| 91 | condition corrected |
| 92 | treated not transported |
| 93 | refused medical aid |
| 94 | treated and transported |
| 95 | triaged at scene no transport |
| 96 | patient gone on arrival |
| CANCEL | cancelled |
| DUP | duplicate incident |
| NOTSNT | unit not sent |
| ZZZZZZ | no disposition |

## Other sources

- **MODZCTA** (`pri4-ifjk`): Modified ZIP Code Tabulation Area polygons. Field `zcta` lists the 5-digit ZCTAs merged into each MODZCTA; used to map incident zips.
- **Facilities Database** (`ji82-xba5`, NYC Planning): records with facility type AMBULANCE STATION or EMERGENCY MEDICAL STATION operated by FDNY are used as known EMS station locations.
- **Open-Meteo historical archive**: hourly temperature (°C), precipitation (mm), snowfall (cm), relative humidity (%) and wind speed (km/h) at Central Park (40.78 N, 73.97 W), local time.
